Build name and address from the ledger

Source: R/md-rollup.R
md_rollup.Rd

Phase 5 step 6 (dev/IDENTITY.md §6). The ledger holds every observation; compile, the statistics, the guards, groups and clusters read name and address. These functions rebuild those two tables from the ledger, in the shape and grain today's ingests write, so everything downstream keeps working:

Usage

md_build_rollups(con)

md_compare_rollups(con)

md_install_rollups(con, keep_legacy = TRUE)

Arguments

con

A DuckDB connection.

keep_legacy

Keep the replaced tables as name_legacy and address_legacy (replacing any earlier legacy copy).

Value

md_build_rollups(): row counts, invisibly.

md_compare_rollups(): a data frame per table, source and class: live rows, rollup rows, and the share of each matched in the other on (EIN, source, light key).

md_install_rollups(): con, invisibly.

Details

md_build_rollups()

Builds rollup_name and rollup_address beside the live tables.

md_compare_rollups()

Row counts per source and class, live against rollup, and how many rows of each find a match in the other.

md_install_rollups()

Swaps the rollups in, keeping the old tables as name_legacy and address_legacy, and rebuilds name_derived and address_derived from the text-keyed columns (md_link_derived()).

Grain and columns

One name row per (ein, source, variant_class, light key) (md_light_key()) with the most frequent spelling, as today's ingests group. One address row per (ein, source, class, paired name, street, city, state, ZIP) under the light key. Every spelling stays in the ledger; these tables are the view compile reads. The columns and source tags are today's (bmf, efile990, schedi, schedr, f1023ez, e_postcard, revocations, meta_address), plus:

name_uid, address_uid

Content-hash ids, the same on every rebuild. name_id and address_id stay integers, because compile joins on them; they are renumbered on each rebuild, and name_derived and address_derived are rebuilt with them, so nothing can be orphaned.

name_text_id, address_text_id

The chosen spelling.

n_periods, n_mentions, n_spells, n_support

The counts of §4. n_support is the one that measures support for that kind: distinct years for a first-party series, rows for mentions (only each filer's latest return for a tax year), spells for a snapshot, NULL for the seed. n_obs is set equal to it, so compile's tiebreak reads a defined quantity rather than today's mix.

What is derived here rather than at ingest

  • former: a 990-header legal name whose last year is before the EIN's latest legal name.

  • A 990-header address is mailing if it is the EIN's most recent, historical otherwise.

  • Guard inputs (n_self_filers, filer_ein_lo, filer_ein_hi), from asserted_by. Run md_guard_observed() after installing.

Only EINs present in entity are kept, as today's ingests do; the count held back is reported. entity itself is not rebuilt: the ledger holds names and addresses, not the BMF's other attributes.

Not carried

The BMF's own lat, lon, county, cbsa, is_po_box and n_vintages are not in the ledger. md_install_rollups() copies them from the live address row with the same EIN, source and spelling; run md_ingest_geocode() after installing, as the build already does, for the census geography.
